Wednesday, November 25

Game recap

VGK5EDM3Final: VGK 5, EDM 3

The Oilers came home to stop the bleeding and needed all of six minutes to reopen it. Jack Eichel scored on the power play at 6:13, Trevor Connelly made it 2-0 unassisted three minutes later, and Edmonton spent the second period climbing back: Colton Dach at 3:03, then Connor McDavid's 14th with 19 seconds left to tie it. The reward for all that work was Nic Dowd, who picked 2:08 of the third for his first goal of the season. Eichel got his second at 5:29, Vasily Podkolzin answered 16 seconds later with his 14th, and Connelly's empty-netter gave him two goals and an assist. Carter Hart made 21 saves on 24 shots, Devon Levi 22 on 26. Vegas is 15-6-5 and three points back of first with a game in hand. Edmonton has dropped four straight after a 17-3-3 start. The Oilers usually wait until June to let everybody down; this year they're getting it done before Thanksgiving.

Tuesday, November 24

Game recap

CBJ2NJD3Final: CBJ 2, NJD 3

Two days after getting the hook in St. Louis, Connor Hellebuyck got the easy shift: 19 saves on 21 shots as the Devils held off Columbus 3-2. New Jersey did its damage early. Timo Meier opened it at 4:59 off the new top line with Jack Hughes and Connor Brown, his goal in a fourth straight game, and Brenden Dillon scored his first of the year three minutes later. Charlie Coyle cut it to 2-1 before the first was out, Brown made it 3-1 in the second, and Mikael Pyyhtia scored shorthanded with 14 seconds left in the period to make it interesting. Then nobody scored for 20 minutes. Zach Werenski logged 30:53 and put six shots on net, Cam Talbot stopped 27 of 30, and the Devils are 16-8-0. Columbus is 9-13-0 and gets the rematch Wednesday at home, where 2.55 goals a game, second-fewest in the league, will have to stretch a little further.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

LAK2MTL1Final: LAK 2, MTL 1

The Kings walked into the Bell Centre at 7-12-2 and walked out with a 2-1 win, which is about the rudest thing a team that low in the Pacific can do to a crowd in Montreal. Darcy Kuemper did most of the work: 29 saves on 30 shots. Alex Laferriere scored on the power play in the first off Quinton Byfield and Artemi Panarin, Alex Newhook tied it in the second, and Trevor Moore scored the winner at 14:57 of the second from Erik Haula and Joel Armia. Then the Canadiens spent a scoreless third finding out Kuemper wasn't moving. Jakub Dobes stopped 20 of 22 for the Canadiens, who have lost two straight and are 5-4-1 in their last 10. Los Angeles is 8-12-2. Montreal is still third in the Atlantic, but losing at home to the Kings is the kind of thing the Bell Centre remembers longer than the standings do.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY1OTT2Final: CGY 1, OTT 2

Calgary outshot Ottawa 36-31 and lost anyway, because Linus Ullmark stopped 35 of them. The Senators got both of their goals in the last eight minutes of the first: Michael Amadio scored unassisted at 12:16, and Shane Pinto made it 2-0 at 17:37 for his 10th. Pinto had a full night. He also dropped the gloves with Joel Hanley at 12:17 of the third, then got to watch Matt Coronato score on the power play at 15:40 to make Ullmark's night a little less peaceful. That was all the Flames had. Devin Cooley stopped 29 of 31 in a game he deserved better from. Ottawa is 16-6-3, first in the Atlantic and 7-1-2 in its last 10. Calgary is 10-13-2 and has scored 2.44 goals a game, which is how you outshoot a team and go home with one goal and a fight to show for it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TOR4NYI2Final: TOR 4, NYI 2

The Maple Leafs won a hockey game. Write down the date. Down 2-0 on Long Island after Anthony Duclair scored in the first and Mathew Barzal got his first goal of the season in the second, Toronto scored four straight for its first win in 10 games. Dakota Joshua got one back in the second, Chris Tanev tied it 3:52 into the third with his first of the year, and Gavin McKenna scored the winner at 8:55 with an extra skater on, his seventh. Easton Cowan put it in the empty net. Auston Matthews' assist on Tanev's goal ran his road point streak to 10 games to open the season, a Leafs record. Anthony Stolarz stopped 20 of 22, Ilya Sorokin 28 of 31. Toronto is 9-14-3, and the Islanders, up two goals in the third at home, managed to make a team that's 1-8-1 in its last 10 look like it had a plan.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA2WPG4Final: UTA 2, WPG 4

Five goals in the first 14 minutes, then one more in the last seven seconds, and Gabriel Vilardi had three of them. Vilardi opened the scoring at 5:11 and put Winnipeg back ahead at 7:26, both off Kyle Connor, with Utah's Andrew Peeke and Lawson Crouse answering each time. Morgan Barron's goal at 14:00 of the first stood as the winner, and Vilardi finished the hat trick into the empty net at 19:53. In between, Utah threw everything at Stuart Skinner, who stopped 34 of 36 while the Jets got 15 shots all night. Sebastian Cossa stopped 11 of 14 for Utah. Winnipeg is 12-9-4 and 8-1-1 in its last 10. Utah is 12-10-3 and 3-4-3 in its last 10. Outshooting a team 36-15 and losing by two is a skill, and the Mammoth have been practicing it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA2SEA3Final: ANA 2, SEA 3

Forty minutes of nothing, then five goals in the third, and Seattle had the last one. Ben Meyers opened it at 2:51, and Cutter Gauthier answered 75 seconds later for his 22nd of the season and his 18th in November, two shy of the NHL record for a calendar month with three games left in it. Vince Dunn put Seattle back ahead, Sam Colangelo tied it at 12:35, and Kaapo Kakko scored the winner at 17:35 off Brandon Montour and Mackie Samoskevich. Joey Daccord stopped 24 of 26. Lukas Dostal stopped 18 of 21 for Anaheim. The Kraken are 11-9-1. The Ducks have lost four straight and are 11-13-1, which means Gauthier is chasing Teemu Selanne and Joe Malone while the rest of the roster chases Gauthier.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN5SJS2Final: MIN 5, SJS 2

Filip Gustavsson made his season debut after hip surgery, the Wild set a franchise record with a point in a 15th straight game, and Jared Spurgeon passed Mikko Koivu for the most games in Wild history at 1,029. San Jose was mostly there to hold the door. The Sharks did lead 2-1 in the first, on a Tyler Toffoli power-play goal and Alexander Wennberg's first of the season, both set up by Macklin Celebrini. Then Brock Faber tied it with 42 seconds left in the period, and Joel Eriksson Ek scored 13 seconds into the second for the winner. Kirill Kaprizov had a goal and two assists, Eriksson Ek and Blake Coleman added empty-netters, and Gustavsson stopped 22 of 24. Yaroslav Askarov stopped 25 of 28. Minnesota is 18-3-5 with 41 points, the most in the league. San Jose is 11-13-2 and got exactly one period of being a problem.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Pickard, 34, went 1-1-1 with an .855 save percentage in three games. He is on a one-year, $1 million deal and would go to AHL Iowa if he clears.

thehockeynews.com ↗

Confirmed · Nov 25: The Wild announced Pickard's assignment to AHL Iowa, Pro Hockey Rumors says, which means he cleared waivers. prohockeyrumors.com ↗

FLA
WaiversNot confirmed by the team

Panthers put Cole Schwindt on waivers a day after losing Reinhardt, Friedman reports

Schwindt is scoreless in 15 games this season and would likely go to AHL Charlotte if he clears. Vancouver claimed Cole Reinhardt off waivers from Florida on Monday.

prohockeyrumors.com ↗

Puckline's Report

The Oilers came home to stop the bleeding and needed all of six minutes to reopen it. Jack Eichel scored on the power play at 6:13, Trevor Connelly made it 2-0 unassisted three minutes later, and Edmonton spent the second period climbing back: Colton Dach at 3:03, then Connor McDavid's 14th with 19 seconds left to tie it. The reward for all that work was Nic Dowd, who picked 2:08 of the third for his first goal of the season. Eichel got his second at 5:29, Vasily Podkolzin answered 16 seconds later with his 14th, and Connelly's empty-netter gave him two goals and an assist. Carter Hart made 21 saves on 24 shots, Devon Levi 22 on 26. Vegas is 15-6-5 and three points back of first with a game in hand. Edmonton has dropped four straight after a 17-3-3 start. The Oilers usually wait until June to let everybody down; this year they're getting it done before Thanksgiving.

By Puckline Prince

WPG @ BOS · 7:00 PM ET

Winnipeg JetsWPG12-9-4 · 28 PTSML +132
@7:00 PM ETWed Nov 25 · TD Garden
WPG +132MLBOS -160
Boston BruinsBOS15-7-1 · 31 PTSML -160

Puckline Preview

The last time these two met, Oct. 2 in Winnipeg, the Jets were 1:38 from a home-opener win until Elias Lindholm tied it with the net empty and JJ Peterka ended it on an overtime breakaway. Lindholm has only gotten ruder since. He scored four on Washington on Saturday, which ties the Bruins' single-game record and gives him 10 points in eight November games. Boston is 15-7-1, and 12 of those 15 wins came by two or more, so this isn't a team that lives on drama. It does live in the penalty box: 13.43 minutes a game, with Nikita Zadorov leading the entire league at 80. Marco Sturm got three days off before this one and said, "I don't like it." James Hagens is back at practice in a non-contact jersey but still on injured reserve.

Winnipeg is the hot team nobody asked for, 8-1-1 in its last 10 right after going nine without a win. Monday the Jets beat Utah 4-2 on 15 shots, three of them Gabriel Vilardi goals, which is either ruthless finishing or the hockey version of finding a twenty in your coat. Mark Scheifele just passed Dale Hawerchuk for the franchise goals record and Kyle Connor has 19 this year. Nico Daws (2-1-0 as a Jet) gets the start across from Jeremy Swayman. The Jets are 0-2-1 in their last three against Boston, outscored 16-7, so the nine-game slump isn't the only thing they'd like to stop talking about.

By Puckline Prince

NYR @ BUF · 7:00 PM ET

New York RangersNYR13-9-1 · 27 PTSML +114
@7:00 PM ETWed Nov 25 · KeyBank Center
NYR +114MLBUF -137
Buffalo SabresBUF10-10-4 · 24 PTSML -137

Puckline Preview

Buffalo comes home from a six-game trip that went 2-3-1 and somehow ended on a high: a 6-2 win in Tampa, 11 days after losing 8-3 to the same Lightning. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen got his 100th win that night, has won two straight starts, and gets the net again, WGR's Paul Hamilton reports. Tage Thompson has 17 goals and has scored in four straight. Jack Quinn has 13. That's 30 of Buffalo's 73, which is less a scoring attack than a carpool. Now the bad news: they're home. The Sabres are 4-6-0 in their own building, where the fans know where the exits are.

The Rangers (13-9-1) bring the No. 1 penalty kill in the league, 90.0%, to meet a Buffalo power play that ranks 29th. Adam Fox has 28 points in 23 career games against the Sabres. New York got outshot 40-27 at home by Carolina on Sunday and lost 5-2, and the last trip here, in October 2025, was a 4-0 Igor Shesterkin shutout. Shesterkin is out for the season, so Joonas Korpisalo (3-0-0, .940) gets this one over Dylan Garand, Mike Sullivan confirmed. Pavel Dorofeyev made the trip but is on NHL.com's injured list for tonight. The New York Post says the Rangers would like to find Matt Rempe a fresh start somewhere else, and Forever Blueshirts says tonight he gets a seat in the press box. Buffalo took the last one, 5-3 at the Garden in April, against a Rangers team that was already eliminated. Somebody had to do it.

By Puckline Prince

CAR @ TBL · 7:00 PM ET

Carolina HurricanesCAR18-3-3 · 39 PTSML -128
@7:00 PM ETWed Nov 25 · Benchmark International Arena
CAR -128MLTBL +106
Tampa Bay LightningTBL15-6-2 · 32 PTSML +106

Puckline Preview

Something has to give: Carolina is 10-2-1 on the road and Tampa Bay is 10-2-0 at home. The Hurricanes, defending champs, are 18-3-3, first in the league at 4.17 goals a game and second in goals against, with a seven-game point streak. Sebastian Aho recently passed Eric Staal for the most goals since the franchise moved to Carolina. Pyotr Kochetkov is 13-1-1, but Brandon Bussi (5-2-2, .879) had the starter's crease at the morning skate and stopped 25 of 27 at the Garden on Sunday, because when your team is this good you can carry an .879 and still mostly get the W. The Hurricanes haven't announced it. Nikolaj Ehlers is out again, so Seth Jarvis moves to the top power play, and that unit (25.6%, sixth) gets a Tampa penalty kill that ranks 24th. K'Andre Miller was under the weather this morning, and Rod Brind'Amour is hopeful he plays.

The Lightning are 15-6-2 and a little testy. Nikita Kucherov, who asked for a trade on Oct. 30, leads them with 32 points, and Jon Cooper sat him, Brayden Point and Jake Guentzel for part of the third period in Sunday's 6-2 loss to Buffalo. Nothing says "please stay" like a seat on the bench. The help looks close: Brandon Hagel (13 goals in 20 games) is off injured reserve and expected to play, NHL.com says, and Pro Hockey Rumors has Zemgus Girgensons back too, though Cooper said he wouldn't decide on either until closer to puck drop. Andrei Vasilevskiy, the projected starter, is 16-7-3 with a .924 against Carolina in his career. The last time the Canes were here, in March, they won 4-2 on a puck that went in off Victor Hedman. At least that one didn't require a benching.

By Puckline Prince

OTT @ FLA · 7:00 PM ET

Ottawa SenatorsOTT16-6-3 · 35 PTSML +108
@7:00 PM ETWed Nov 25 · Amerant Bank Arena
OTT +108MLFLA -130
Florida PanthersFLA13-8-3 · 29 PTSML -130

Puckline Preview

Brady Tkachuk's old team comes to his new house. The first one, Oct. 21 in Ottawa, was the big return: he got booed, scored on the power play, and then watched the Senators put up the next five in a 5-1 win, with Bokondji Imama and Hayden Hodgson fighting five seconds after his goal and Ridly Greig and Sam Bennett going later. Since then Ottawa has climbed to first in the Atlantic at 16-6-3 with points in nine straight, its longest run since 2015. Linus Ullmark is 12-1-0 with a .941 and has won six straight, and Jake Sanderson calls him the best goalie in the world right now. The Senators need him to be, because their power play is 12-for-92, dead last. At 13.0% they might as well decline the penalties.

Florida (13-8-3) might finally look like Florida. Aleksander Barkov, out since Oct. 1, and Brad Marchand, out since Oct. 6, are both in tonight, Paul Maurice says, with Jacob Markstrom in goal. Matthew Tkachuk leads the team with 32 points and is expected to play after skipping Sunday's practice. Bennett is coming off a hat trick and a four-point night against Buffalo. Brady has 58 penalty minutes, second in the league, so he's kept busy. The Panthers are 6-3-0 at home with the No. 5 penalty kill, which against this Ottawa power play feels like bringing a fire truck to a birthday candle.

By Puckline Prince

STL @ NYI · 7:00 PM ET

St Louis BluesSTL13-9-2 · 28 PTSML +102
@7:00 PM ETWed Nov 25 · UBS Arena
STL +102MLNYI -122
New York IslandersNYI11-7-5 · 27 PTSML -122

Puckline Preview

The Blues have forgotten how to play a boring game. They've won four straight and scored at least five in all of them: 8-6 over Anaheim, 5-2 in Pittsburgh, 9-6 over New Jersey with five Jake Neighbours assists, and Sunday's 5-4 shootout win over Edmonton, when they erased a three-goal deficit in the last 10 minutes of regulation, a franchise first. Robert Thomas, the league's first star of the week, rested Tuesday and is expected to play. Jimmy Snuggerud (14 goals) and Pavel Buchnevich are out, Blues broadcaster Chris Kerber reports, and The Hockey News says neither made the trip. Brandon Carlo and Connor McMichael are on injured reserve, so The Hockey News has recalls Otto Stenberg and Adam Jiricek going in, with Calle Rosen the projected scratch. Joel Hofer (.920) is the likely starter, though Jordan Binnington has proven you can allow six and win, because he did it twice last week.

The Islanders led Toronto 2-0 on Monday, at home, against a team that hadn't won in nine games, and lost 4-2. That ended a seven-game point streak and presumably several TV remotes. They do start fast: Anthony Duclair leads the NHL with six game-opening goals, and New York is 9-1-4 when it scores first. Finishing is the trouble, especially with a power play at 16.7%, 29th. Kyle Palmieri is on injured reserve, Ryan Pulock is out a week or two, and Calum Ritchie is up from Hamilton and will play, per NHL.com. Before the game they honor Casey Cizikas for 1,000 NHL games, every one of them for the Islanders, which takes a kind of loyalty the rest of us reserve for family and bad cars.

By Puckline Prince

CGY @ PIT · 7:00 PM ET

Calgary FlamesCGY10-13-2 · 22 PTSML +134
@7:00 PM ETWed Nov 25 · PPG Paints Arena
CGY +134MLPIT -162
Pittsburgh PenguinsPIT7-14-2 · 16 PTSML -162

Puckline Preview

If you like goals, there are 13 other games tonight. Calgary scores 2.44 a game, last in the NHL, and is 10-13-2. It outshot Ottawa on Monday and lost 2-1. The strange part is a power play clicking at 26.7%, fifth in the league, which suggests the Flames know how to score and just prefer an advantage. Ryan Huska's request for this one: "We've got to play the full meal deal." He'll have to order it without Morgan Frost, who was hurt Monday and won't play, NHL.com reports. Arturs Silovs (.878) starts for Pittsburgh and Dustin Wolf (.877) is the projected Flame, so the shooters have a chance to feel good about themselves.

The Penguins are 7-14-2, have lost four straight and have three regulation wins, tied with Vancouver for the fewest in the league. On Sunday they put 33 shots on Jake Oettinger and lost 1-0. Sidney Crosby told the Post-Gazette on Tuesday he hopes to finish his career in Pittsburgh, which is either the most romantic sentence in sports or a cry for a better supporting cast. Evgeni Malkin, 40, is available after missing two games, the team says, and NHL.com projects him on Crosby's line, but Egor Chinakhov is out with no timeframe. Erik Karlsson leads the team with 19 points and, if you believe the rumor mill, in spots on other teams' wish lists. Calgary won here 2-1 in January. Don't expect them to apologize for the sequel.

PHI @ WSH · 7:00 PM ET

Philadelphia FlyersPHI9-11-6 · 24 PTSML +130
@7:00 PM ETWed Nov 25 · Capital One Arena
PHI +130MLWSH -156
Washington CapitalsWSH10-11-0 · 20 PTSML -156

Puckline Preview

The Capitals have lost five straight, all in regulation, and given up 30 goals doing it. Five or more against in five straight games hadn't happened to them since October 1993. They're 2-7-0 in November, and after the 7-5 loss in Boston they were rewarded with two long, demanding practices. Logan Thompson goes back in net, RMNB reports, with an .841 save percentage this month. Alex Ovechkin just passed Nicklas Backstrom for the most assists in team history, which would be a lovelier story if his goal drought, already the longest of his career, hadn't kept going Saturday. Jordan Kyrou is out this week, Anthony Beauvillier is expected back, and Vincent Desharnais misses a 13th straight game. Washington has won six straight at home against Philadelphia, including 5-2 on Oct. 28, when Kyrou and Alex Tuch scored twice each.

After that one, Sean Couturier said of his own team, "At times this year, we're soft, I would say." The Flyers are 9-11-6 and suddenly a bit crunchy: three straight wins, including a comeback from three down in the third in Ottawa and Noah Cates' winner with 30 seconds left in Montreal. A fourth would be their first streak that long since February 2024. Matvei Michkov leads them with 11 goals and 20 points, Rick Tocchet says he likes Denver Barkey at center, and Porter Martone hasn't scored since Oct. 24. Joseph Woll gets the start over Dan Vladar, RMNB reports. Philadelphia is 30th in goals and Washington is 30th in goals against, so tonight we learn which of them is better at being bad.

NJD @ CBJ · 7:00 PM ET

New Jersey DevilsNJD16-8-0 · 32 PTSML -154
@7:00 PM ETWed Nov 25 · Nationwide Arena
NJD -154MLCBJ +128
Columbus Blue JacketsCBJ9-13-0 · 18 PTSML +128

Puckline Preview

Same teams, different arena, two days later. The Devils won Monday's half of the home-and-home 3-2, with Connor Hellebuyck making 19 saves two days after he was pulled in St. Louis. He's 8-1-0 since coming to New Jersey, and Timo Meier has goals in four straight. Brenden Dillon even scored, his first in 73 games, so check the basement for water damage. New Jersey is 16-8-0 and 12-0-0 when it leads after two. The hole in the boat is the penalty kill: 65.5%, 30th in the league, and after Tuesday's practice Dougie Hamilton and Cody Glass both said the special teams need work. They let Columbus score shorthanded on Monday too, with 14 seconds left in the second, which is the kind of thing that gets a power play its own meeting.

Columbus is 9-13-0, and like New Jersey and Washington it has no loser points at all, the only three teams in the league that can say that. The Blue Jackets score 2.55 a game, 31st. Zach Werenski played 30:53 on Monday with six shots and has a point in all 10 of his road games, a start only five other defensemen have matched. Unhelpfully, this one is at home, where Columbus is 6-6-0. Mathieu Olivier went on injured reserve Tuesday and Conor Garland is there already, but Sean Monahan returns after missing five games, Rick Bowness says. Cam Talbot gets a fifth straight start, per TSN, which expects Hellebuyck at the other end. Give the Jackets this much: in a league that hands out points for losing, they've refused every single one.

By Puckline Prince

VAN @ DET · 7:30 PM ET

Vancouver CanucksVAN6-19-1 · 13 PTSML +188
@7:30 PM ETWed Nov 25 · Little Caesars Arena
VAN +188MLDET -230
Detroit Red WingsDET8-12-3 · 19 PTSML -230

Puckline Preview

Detroit plays its first game since the Dylan Larkin saga finally ended with a trade to Montreal, and Kirby Dach makes his Red Wings debut centering the third line. Andrew Copp, on the mood: "It'll be nice to just move on from the whole situation." Great news, Andrew, there's a spare. Simon Edvinsson is still unsigned with a Dec. 1 deadline, and Pierre LeBrun reports Detroit has told teams it'll sit on him all year if its price isn't met. Interim GM Shawn Horcoff says this isn't a rebuild. The Wings are 8-12-3, have lost two straight and have missed the playoffs 10 years running, the longest drought in the league, so call it what you like. Sam Montembeault, also from the Larkin deal, is practicing but still on injured reserve, and Daniil Tarasov (.927) gets the net over John Gibson (.862), MLive's Ansar Khan reports.

The Canucks are 6-19-1 and allow 4.38 goals a game, worst in hockey, with the worst penalty kill too, 61.2%. Detroit's is 29th, so the first team to take a bad penalty should simply apologize. Brock Boeser's point streak is at 11 games, the longest by a Canuck since 2023-24. Elias Pettersson, the forward, has gone home to Vancouver after seeing a specialist and will miss the whole four-game trip; Elias Pettersson, the defenseman, is projected in. Leevi Meriläinen is expected in goal. Detroit won the first meeting 5-2 on Oct. 22, when Vancouver managed 13 shots and none at all in the second period. Twenty minutes, zero shots. A lamppost would have had a chance at one.

By Puckline Prince

NSH @ DAL · 8:00 PM ET

Nashville PredatorsNSH12-6-5 · 29 PTSML +142
@8:00 PM ETWed Nov 25 · American Airlines Center
NSH +142MLDAL -172
Dallas StarsDAL15-6-2 · 32 PTSML -172

Puckline Preview

The Stars have won five straight by the skin of somebody's teeth: 2-0, then 2-1 in overtime, 4-3 in overtime, 4-3 in a shootout, and Sunday's 1-0 over Pittsburgh on 23 shots. One of those was the night in Vegas when they trailed 3-1 with 78 seconds left. Jake Oettinger leads the league with five shutouts and is 13-4-1, which explains most of it. Dallas is 15-6-2 while ranking 25th in goals, and three points ahead of Nashville and Colorado in the Central. Tyler Myers returns tonight after missing three games, NHL.com reports, while Oskar Back is still on its injured list. Lian Bichsel and Kyle Capobianco are still out, so Kyle Burroughs stays on the third pair, projected next to Myers.

Nashville (12-6-5) ended a two-game skid Saturday, beating Pittsburgh 4-3 on Jayden Struble's third-period goal, with Juuse Saros leaving for a couple of minutes to get a skate blade fixed and coming back to win it. The Predators won seven in a row before that skid, and Mavrik Bourque visits the team that traded him in July. They took the first meeting 2-1 on Oct. 3, when Miro Heiskanen scored 47 seconds in for Dallas and Nashville answered with two power-play goals and then nobody scored for 44 minutes. Expect more of the same: these are the No. 2 and No. 3 penalty kills in hockey, 89.1% and 88.8%. Pierre LeBrun lists Ryan O'Reilly among the names to watch in trades but says he likely doesn't want to leave. Watching these two try to score, you'd understand if he wanted a nap.

By Puckline Prince

UTA @ MIN · 8:00 PM ET

Utah MammothUTA12-10-3 · 27 PTSML +125
@8:00 PM ETWed Nov 25 · Grand Casino Arena
UTA +125MLMIN -150
Minnesota WildMIN18-3-5 · 41 PTSML -150

Puckline Preview

The Wild have points in 15 straight games (12-0-3), a franchise record, and Kirill Kaprizov has a point in all 15, also a franchise record. He's up to 49 points on the season, second only to Connor McDavid. Jared Spurgeon broke Mikko Koivu's games-played record Monday. At this point Minnesota's equipment staff just walks around with a plaque. The Wild are 18-3-5, lead the league with 41 points, allow the fewest goals (2.23 a game) and haven't lost in regulation at home, 6-0-2. Filip Gustavsson won his season debut Monday, but the net goes back to Jesper Wallstedt (16-2-4, .924), per the team. Quinn Hughes is on injured reserve and can't return before Friday. And Pierre LeBrun says they still want a top-six forward, because apparently this is the version that needs help.

Utah is 2-4-3 in its last nine and has spent the week conducting a study on shots. Saturday the Mammoth beat Anaheim with 12 of them. Monday they outshot Winnipeg 36-15 and lost. Dylan Guenther came back for that one after two weeks out, and the power play is third in the league at 31.8%, but Nick Schmaltz, John Marino and half the blue line are unavailable, so Zac Jones is up on defense. Sebastian Cossa has started the last three, but NHL.com projects Karel Vejmelka tonight and the team hasn't said. The first meeting, a 3-1 Wild win on Oct. 27, had three fights, including Mikhail Sergachev and Matt Boldy, and Utah lost the special teams battle 2-0. The last time the Mammoth played in this building, in March, they lost 5-0, so a fight or two might be the most competitive option.

By Puckline Prince

MTL @ COL · 9:30 PM ET

Montreal CanadiensMTL14-7-4 · 32 PTSML +110
@9:30 PM ETWed Nov 25 · Ball Arena
MTL +110MLCOL -132
Colorado AvalancheCOL13-7-3 · 29 PTSML -132

Puckline Preview

Dylan Larkin takes his new No. 89 on the road for the first time. His Canadiens debut Monday came with an assist, 19:57 of ice and a 2-1 loss to the Kings, and the welcome gift is a spot on the first power-play unit, which is a bit like being handed the keys to a car with no engine. Montreal's power play is 10-for-73, 13.7%, 31st in the league. The Canadiens (14-7-4) have lost four of six, but they're 9-2-1 on the road and their goalies travel well: Jacob Fowler is 10-3-2 with a .918 and would be next up, though nobody's been named. Ivan Demidov, Mike Matheson, Chris Kreider and Josh Anderson all stayed home. David Reinbacher and Brett Berard came up from Laval for the trip.

Colorado hasn't played since Thursday, when it beat Anaheim 4-0 and ended Cutter Gauthier's 10-game goal streak. The big question got answered this morning: Cale Makar took part in the skate and returns tonight after a three-game absence, NHL.com reports. Nathan MacKinnon won't be back for about 12 weeks. The Avalanche have handled it better than anyone had a right to, starting with Nov. 14 in Montreal, when they won 4-1 without both of them and ended a 12-game Canadiens point streak. Former Canadien Artturi Lehkonen scored that night and leads Colorado with 15 goals, in case Montreal needed another thing to think about. The Avs are 8-1-2 at home and second in the league at 3.91 goals a game. Last season these two traded a 7-2 and a 7-3, so bring a snack and a backup goalie.

CHI @ SEA · 9:40 PM ET

Chicago BlackhawksCHI8-14-2 · 18 PTSML +138
@9:40 PM ETWed Nov 25 · Climate Pledge Arena
CHI +138MLSEA -166
Seattle KrakenSEA11-9-1 · 23 PTSML -166

Puckline Preview

Chicago started the season 0-8-1 on the road and is now one win from a perfect three-game trip, all of it without Connor Bedard, who had shoulder surgery Monday and is out about four months. The Blackhawks are 4-1-1 in their last six. Roman Kantserov had his first NHL hat trick and a fourth point in Vancouver on Sunday, Frank Nazar has a six-game point streak, and Patrick Kane, 38, has one going at five. Anton Frondell practiced in full Tuesday and Jeff Blashill is hoping he plays; Luke Glendening looks set for his Blackhawks debut; Wyatt Kaiser serves the second game of his suspension. The Sun-Times has Spencer Knight likely in net. Chicago is still 8-14-2 and minus-32, so let's hold off on the parade route.

The matchup of the night, if you enjoy suffering: the Blackhawks have scored on the power play in six straight games, and Seattle's penalty kill is 62.1%, 31st in the league. Coach Lane Lambert called it "the elephant in the room." On Monday the elephant left long enough for the Kraken to kill a four-minute double minor against Anaheim, and Kaapo Kakko won it 3-2 with 2:25 left. Joey Daccord stopped 24 of 26 that night after being pulled in his previous two starts; whether he or Philipp Grubauer goes tonight hasn't been announced. Freddy Gaudreau is expected to play his 500th NHL game. Jared McCann is still out, a month into the 10 weeks the Kraken announced in October. It's the first meeting this season. Chicago won the last one here, 4-2 in April, back when neither of them was going anywhere either.

By Puckline Prince

SJS @ ANA · 10:00 PM ET

San Jose SharksSJS11-13-2 · 24 PTSML +116
@10:00 PM ETWed Nov 25 · Honda Center
SJS +116MLANA -140
Anaheim DucksANA11-13-1 · 23 PTSML -140

Puckline Preview

Cutter Gauthier is chasing history and the Ducks are chasing a point. Gauthier has 18 goals in 12 November games, two short of the NHL record for a month, shared by Joe Malone (1921) and Teemu Selanne (1993), with three November games left counting tonight. He has 22 on the year. Around him, Anaheim just went 0-4 on the road: 8-6 in St. Louis, 4-0 in Colorado, then a pair of 3-2 losses. Joel Quenneville's review of the last one: "Terrible loss. Tough loss." The power play leads the league at 33.3% and still managed one shot on a four-minute double minor in Seattle. Leo Carlsson, hurt in a collision with a linesman in Utah, sat out Monday and is day to day with no word on tonight, and Beckett Sennecke is on injured reserve. Neither team has named a goalie.

The Sharks (11-13-2) are one point up, third in the Pacific with a minus-23 goal differential, which tells you plenty about the Pacific. Macklin Celebrini leads them with 31 points and has 15 in his last 10 games; two more assists Monday gave him 33 multi-assist games, passing Ron Francis for sixth-most by a player 21 or younger. The problem is a penalty kill that has allowed a goal in 10 straight games, walking into the best power play in hockey. Jacob Trouba and Kiefer Sherwood are out. These two met twice in September: Ducks 6-2, then Sharks 10-0. It was only preseason, but somebody in Anaheim's goal remembers. The Ducks won the last real one 6-1 in April, so going by precedent, the goalies should bring sunscreen.

By Puckline Prince
